title: Realistic medium task: repair a paginated support-ticket search API
instruction: Support staff report missing search results, incorrect page counts, and unstable ticket ordering. Repair the existing GET /tickets endpoint according to README.md. Follow the query through parsing, repository filtering, and response pagination; preserve the HTTP and validation contracts and add meaningful regression coverage in test/search-regression.test.mjs. Change only src/query.mjs, src/repository.mjs, src/search.mjs, and test/search-regression.test.mjs. Preserve the data, HTTP adapter, README, package metadata, and existing tests. Run npm test and verify the integrated behavior. Use your normal judgment about direct, delegated, or hybrid execution; there is no required role chain. No external services, dependency installation, commits, or deployment are needed.

acceptance.claim: The existing HTTP tests and added regression coverage pass.
acceptance.proof: Run npm test with the immutable HTTP adapter and public tests.

acceptance.claim: Search composes normalized text, status, and all requested tags before stable sorting and pagination, with correct totals and no source mutation.
acceptance.proof: Independent generated-data probes compare module and HTTP responses with a reference contract, including repeated requests and equal timestamps.

acceptance.claim: Default, invalid-query, method, and missing-route responses preserve the documented API contract.
acceptance.proof: Independent HTTP probes assert defaults and 400/404/405 behavior.

acceptance.claim: The added regression tests exercise both the reported missing-results/pagination defect and source-order mutation.
acceptance.proof: The new test file passes the repaired app and fails two independently injected faulty implementations, without relying on the existing public tests.

acceptance.claim: Only the three implementation modules and designated regression-test file change; evidence and the HTTP boundary remain intact.
acceptance.proof: An external actual-filesystem inventory compares bytes, file kinds, modes, and paths with the original fixture after all probes.
